policy_text:
[Routing Policy v3: Hard constraints + Scorecard + Tie-break]
Goal:
- Maximize the FINAL best OBP score found within budget (best-of-run).
- Avoid catastrophic failures (very low scores / frequent failures).
- Keep routing interpretable.

Signals (from input):
- operator ∈ {E1,E2,M1,M2,UNKNOWN}
- has_error (bool), n_chars, n_lines, code_density, markers
- fix_score, explore_score
- prior_stats (per-operator mean score and fail count per backend; higher mean is better, lower fail is better)

Decision procedure:
1) Hard constraints:
   - If has_error=true -> prefer backend A (debugging strength).
   - If code_density > 0.8 AND n_chars > 2000 -> prefer backend B (long-context strength).
   - If prior_stats.fail_count > 3 AND prior_stats.mean_score < -3000 for this operator -> exclude backend (catastrophic).
   - If markers > 15 AND explore_score > 0 -> boost backend C (exploration strength).
   - If n_chars > 2500 AND code_density > 0.9 -> strongly prefer backend B (global restructuring).
   - If operator=E1 AND markers > 20 AND n_chars > 1800 AND code_density > 0.7 -> boost backend C (high-upside exploration).
   - If operator=M1 OR operator=M2 AND prior_stats.fail_count > 2 AND prior_stats.mean_score < -4000 -> exclude backend C (catastrophic for modification tasks).
2) Scorecard:
   For each backend compute:
   Score = Wop + Wlen + Wdensity + Wfix + Wexplore + Wprior + Wrisk + Wcost
   - Wprior: prefer higher mean_score and lower fail_count in prior_stats for this operator.
   - Wrisk: penalize backends with fail_count > 1 for this operator (moderate penalty).
   - Wexplore: if explore_score > 0 OR markers > 10 -> boost backend C (exploration strength).
   - Wcost: small boost for backend C (low cost) when confidence < 0.7.
   - Wcatastrophe: if prior_stats.mean_score < -4000 AND prior_stats.fail_count > 2 for this operator -> exclude backend.
   - Wimprove: if operator=E1/E2 AND markers > 20 AND n_chars > 1800 AND code_density > 0.7 -> boost backend C (high-upside exploration).
   - Wstability: if operator=M1/M2 AND n_chars < 1500 AND markers < 15 -> boost backend A (reliable local edits).
3) Tie-break (when top-2 scores within 0.2):
   - Prefer backend with lower fail_count, then higher mean_score, then cheaper backend.
4) Output JSON: {backend, confidence, reason}.

Output JSON (STRICT):
{"backend": "A"|"B"|"C", "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "reason": "cite 2-3 signals and a profile trait"}.

history.rationale: This update improves best-of-run by: 1) Adding explicit catastrophic exclusion rule (fail_count>3 AND mean_score<-3000) to prevent repeated failures while allowing exploration, 2) Strengthening exploration routing with explicit markers>10 condition based on observed correlation between high markers and successful C usage, 3) Making long-context rule more precise (code_density>0.8 AND n_chars>2000) to better match B's strengths, 4) Adding cost consideration for low-confidence decisions to leverage C's budget efficiency for exploration.
changes: Added explicit catastrophic exclusion: fail_count>3 AND mean_score<-3000 excludes backend
Enhanced exploration routing: markers>10 now boosts backend C
Precise long-context rule: code_density>0.8 AND n_chars>2000
Added cost tie-break for low-confidence decisions
Clarified backend labels (A,B,C instead of names)

history.rationale: This update improves best-of-run by: 1) Adding explicit high-upside rules for backend C when markers>15 AND explore_score>0 (correlates with improvement events), 2) Strengthening backend B preference for very dense/long contexts (n_chars>2500 AND code_density>0.9) to prevent catastrophic -5000 scores, 3) Adding Wcatastrophe exclusion for backends with mean_score<-4000 AND fail_count>2 to prevent repeated failures while allowing moderate-risk exploration, 4) Adding Wimprove rule to selectively boost backend C for E1/E2 operators with high markers and length where it has shown success (-2091.8 s
changes: Added hard constraint: markers>15 AND explore_score>0 boosts backend C for high-exploration tasks
Added hard constraint: n_chars>2500 AND code_density>0.9 strongly prefers backend B for extreme long-context cases
Added Wcatastrophe scorecard component to exclude backends with mean_score<-4000 AND fail_count>2
Added Wimprove scorecard component to boost backend C for E1/E2 operators with markers>20 AND n_chars>1800
Clarified catastrophic exclusion uses mean_score<-4000 threshold (more conservative than -3000)

history.rationale: This policy improves best-of-run by: 1) Targeting backend C for high-upside E1/E2 tasks (markers>20, n_chars>1800, density>0.7) where it achieved -2091.8 scores, 2) Preventing catastrophic failures by excluding C for M1/M2 when prior stats show fail_count>2 AND mean_score<-4000 (observed -5000 failures), 3) Adding stability rule for M1/M2 small tasks to use reliable backend A, 4) Maintaining exploration budget for risky-but-high-upside backend C only in favorable conditions.
changes: Added explicit high-upside rule: operator=E1 AND markers>20 AND n_chars>1800 AND code_density>0.7 -> boost backend C
Added catastrophic prevention rule: operator=M1/M2 AND prior_stats.fail_count>2 AND prior_stats.mean_score<-4000 -> exclude backend C
Added stability rule: operator=M1/M2 AND n_chars<1500 AND markers<15 -> boost backend A
Refined Wimprove condition to require code_density>0.7 for E1/E2 exploration
Clarified catastrophic exclusion uses AND condition (fail_count>2 AND mean_score<-4000)
